title: Zhongzheng Walk: Chiang Kai-shek Hall to 228 Peace Park
excerpt: A 5km self-guided walk through Zhongzheng from Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall past the East Gate, the Taipei Guest House and the Presidential Office Building to the National Taiwan Museum and 228 Peace Memorial Park.
content:
A walk for architecture and history buffs. It starts at Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall and heads north through Zhongzheng, the old administrative heart of Taipei, past the East Gate, the colonial-era hospital, the Taipei Guest House, the Presidential Office Building and the City God Temple, before finishing with the two buildings of the National Taiwan Museum and 228 Peace Memorial Park. The route is about 5km on foot, and depending on how long you spend at the Memorial Hall and the museum it takes roughly 5 to 7 hours.

Tuesday to Sunday are the days to go, ideally setting off in the morning. On Mondays the National Taiwan Museum, its Land Bank Exhibition Hall and the Taipei 228 Memorial Hall are all shut.

If you'd like to coincide with the raising or lowering of the flag on Liberty Square, it goes up at 06:30 and comes down at 17:10 from October to March, and at 06:00 and 18:10 from April to September. The Memorial Hall page has more on the ceremonies.

The Route

To sleep close to the end of the route, the Taipei Main Station hotel guide covers the area one stop north of NTU Hospital.

Step-By-Step

  • 1 Take the red or green line to Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall station and leave by exit 5, which comes up on Aiguo East Road near the south-west corner of the grounds
  • Walk into Liberty Square and visit Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall
    • The hall is free and open daily from 09:00 to 18:00; the grounds are open from 05:00 until midnight
    • Make sure to visit the museum and galleries in the base of the hall
    • The changing of the guard now takes place outdoors on Democracy Boulevard, hourly between 09:00 and 17:00, and it doesn't go ahead in rain
    • Have a look inside the performance halls, the National Theater and National Concert Hall on either side of the square
    • Enjoy the gardens and trail
  • [optional] Try a bubble tea at Chun Shui Tang, the chain that claims to have invented it. Its branch is inside the National Concert Hall, by gate 2, and opens daily from 11:30 to 20:50, so it won't be serving yet if you arrive first thing
  • Leave the square through the Gate of Integrity, the large white arch, and walk north up Zhongshan South Road
  • 2 Pass the East Gate, one of the old city gates of Taipei, which now stands on a traffic island where Ketagalan Boulevard meets Zhongshan South Road
  • 3 Carry on north to walk past the red-brick old building of National Taiwan University Hospital, dating from the Japanese era and still a working hospital
  • 4 [optional] Visit the Taipei Guest House if it's open
    • Most of the year it's hidden behind its walls, but it opens to the public on one or two Saturdays a month from 09:00 to 16:00, with last entry at 15:30
    • The remaining 2026 dates are 7 November and 5 December, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs cancels dates at short notice for official business or typhoons, as it did on 24 October 2026
    • Entry is free and there's no need to book
  • 5 Walk past the Ministry of Foreign Affairs building on Ketagalan Boulevard
  • Walk through Jieshou Park and along the side of the Presidential Office Building
    • On weekdays you can go inside from 09:00 to 12:00 (last entry 11:30); only the ground-floor exhibitions and corridors are open
    • On a handful of Saturdays it opens more fully from 09:00 to 16:00, including the main entrance hall and the great hall. In the rest of 2026 these are 7 November and 5 December, the same days as the Guest House
    • The visitor entrance is gate 3, at the corner of Baoqing Road and Boai Road, which the route passes
    • Entry is free, but you'll need a photo ID (bring your passport), and large bags and video cameras aren't allowed in
  • Follow Chongqing South Road north
  • 6 Turn left into Wuchang Street to see the Taiwan Provincial City God Temple, open daily from 06:30 to 21:00
    • It was first built in 1881 as the city god temple of Taipei Prefecture, then demolished under Japanese rule and rebuilt here after the Second World War
  • 7 Walk east to the corner of Xiangyang Road and Guanqian Road and visit the Land Bank Exhibition Hall of the National Taiwan Museum, which the museum now calls its Paleontology Hall
    • Dinosaur skeletons and fossils fill the main hall, and you can step inside the old bank vault; the museum's own listing for the fossil exhibition runs to 31 December 2026
    • A NT$30 ticket covers both this hall and the main building on the same day
    • Over-65s go free on weekdays, and children under six always go free
  • [optional] There are a few places to eat and drink around this area
  • See the vintage steam locomotives, among the earliest used in Taiwan, under glass outside the main museum building, over the road
  • 8 Visit the National Taiwan Museum main building
    • Opening hours are 09:30 to 17:00, Tuesday to Sunday, and ticket sales end at 16:30
    • It's closed on Mondays, on Lunar New Year's Eve and on the first day of Lunar New Year
  • 9 Enter the 228 Peace Memorial Park behind the museum
  • [optional] Visit the Taipei 228 Memorial Hall to learn about the February 28 incident
    • It's in the old radio station building on the park's southern edge, on Ketagalan Boulevard
    • Open Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00 to 17:00, and entry is now free

Where to Eat

  • Jin Feng Braised Pork Rice is the very popular and famous local restaurant beside exit 2 of Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall station. Recent listings give its hours as 11:00 to 01:00 from Tuesday to Saturday and 11:00 to 23:00 on Sunday, with Mondays off, so it suits lunch before the walk or dinner after it, though queues are common
  • Chun Shui Tang, inside the National Concert Hall, serves noodles, rice dishes and snacks as well as its pearl milk tea, from 11:30 every day
  • Nanmen Market, rebuilt and reopened in 2023 next to the same exit 2, is a daytime food market with cooked-food counters; it closes at around 19:00, and one source lists it as closed on Mondays
  • The middle stretch, from the East Gate to the City God Temple, passes mainly government buildings and the hospital, so eat before you leave Liberty Square or wait until you reach the museum area

Best Time to Go

Tuesday to Sunday all suit this route. On a Monday the Land Bank Exhibition Hall, the National Taiwan Museum and the Taipei 228 Memorial Hall are all closed, which removes the indoor half of the second part of the route. Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall, the City God Temple and the park are open every day.

Start in the morning. If you want to go inside the Presidential Office Building on a weekday, you need to reach gate 3 by 11:30, so keep the Memorial Hall visit short or start at 09:00 when the hall opens. The best days of all are the Saturdays when the Presidential Office and the Taipei Guest House are both fully open, which in the rest of 2026 are 7 November and 5 December; the Presidential Office has already published its 2027 dates, but the Guest House hasn't.

Both government buildings close to visitors on public holidays and when the city suspends work for a typhoon, and the changing of the guard is cancelled in rain. For the flag lowering and the floodlit buildings at dusk, finish the walk and head back to Liberty Square for 17:10 in winter or 18:10 in summer.

Getting There and Back

Start: Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall station (red and green lines), exit 5, on Aiguo East Road beside Liberty Square. Exit 2 is the one for Jin Feng and Nanmen Market.

Finish: NTU Hospital station (red line), whose exits 1 and 4 are inside 228 Peace Memorial Park. Taipei Main Station is one stop north, or about ten minutes on foot up Guanqian Road. The MRT guide explains fares and ticket options.

Alternatively, you could walk back south to Chiang Kai-shek Liberty Square, about 15 minutes from the park, to catch the lowering of the flag and see the magnificent structures by night, or even see a show or concert at one of the performance halls. Then take the MRT back from Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall station, or try for a table at Jin Feng on the way.

Common Questions

How long does the Zhongzheng walk take?

The walking itself is about 5km, a little over an hour at a steady pace, because the line on the map includes a loop around the Memorial Hall grounds. With time inside the hall, the museum buildings and the park, plan on five to seven hours.

Can I go inside the Presidential Office Building?

Yes, on weekday mornings from 09:00 to 12:00, with last entry at 11:30, when the ground-floor exhibitions are open. On a few Saturdays a year more of the building opens from 09:00 to 16:00. It's free, individuals don't need to book, and everyone must show photo ID and go through a security check at gate 3.

When is the Taipei Guest House open?

Only on selected Saturdays, roughly one or two a month, from 09:00 to 16:00 with last entry at 15:30. Its official site publishes the dates for the year and posts cancellations, which happen for official business and bad weather. Outside those days you can only see the walls and gates from the street.

Is the walk worth doing on a Monday?

Only partly. Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall, the Presidential Office's weekday opening and the City God Temple are all available, but the two National Taiwan Museum buildings and the Taipei 228 Memorial Hall are closed every Monday.

How much does the walk cost?

Very little. The Memorial Hall, the Presidential Office, the Guest House, the temple, the park and the Taipei 228 Memorial Hall are all free. The only ticket is NT$30 for the National Taiwan Museum, which covers both its main building and the Land Bank Exhibition Hall on the same day.

Carry On Walking

The Daan walking route finishes at Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall station, where this one starts, so the two link up into a longer day. From 228 Peace Memorial Park, Ximen is about 15 minutes' walk west for the Wanhua heritage walk, and the North Gate a similar distance north-west for the Dadaocheng and Dihua Street walk.
